test.name: German immigration to Pennsylvania in the 1840s
test.description: Regression test for issue #1315: wiki-derived historical context must cite the source page URL, not just the article title. Uses the skill's own worked SKILL.md example topic (German immigration, Pennsylvania, 1840s).

input.user_message: My ancestor immigrated from Germany to Pennsylvania around 1845. What historical context should I know about German immigration during that period, and how does it affect my research?

judge_context: This test's primary purpose is the Citation completeness dimension: the response must end with a "Sources consulted"-style list naming every wiki/Wikipedia page it actually drew from, each with its real URL (`source_url` on `wiki_search` results, `url` from `wiki_read`/`wikipedia_search`) — not just the article title. Grade that end-of-response list, not scattered inline citation. Do not let an unrelated Source quality concern (e.g. a claim stated too confidently) pull this dimension down.

Should connect the historical context to research-useful facts — for example, that German civil registration was not national and church records (Kirchenbücher) are the primary pre-civil-registration source, or that identifying the specific German town/parish of origin is essential before searching German archives.
Should not just summarize 'many Germans immigrated in the 1840s' — the value of this skill is in surfacing context the genealogist can act on, not general encyclopedia content.
